### `afkconvoy help example-run`

The team [`afkconvoy help example`](help:example) reads file by file, pushed, bound to a repo and run. First what must be in place; then one issue of its `fix` workflow, followed from its flow label to the base branch, with how long each stage took and what it cost.

## Before a fleet works with it

`check` accepts the team as written, once it is pushed: it reads a role from GitHub. Three skills that the fellow's and the attending's own skills say to load are other authors' and are not written. Each role's `skills-lock.json` names them and where each is from: add them in each of the two directories, and commit them.

```sh
npx skills add <source> --skill <name> --agent claude-code
```

Until then `skills-loaded.sh` refuses every `pass` and `reject` of those two roles, and the attending's `limits.ts` does under pi. The hooks call `jq`: every host of the fleet needs it.

The roster lets the attending run pi first, so a host whose host kit holds pi needs `pi`, logged in to the provider of its model: `openai-codex/gpt-5.5`, as written — `afkconvoy kit` adds it to the host kit, and probes it. Write another model pi lists — or take pi out of the attending's entry, and it runs Claude Code as the others do. A host kit holding pi on a host without it starts nothing: `plan`, `tick` and `run` refuse, `doctor` finds the same, and each names the range that calls for it and the line that installs it:

```text
pi is not installed, called for by the range of the role `attending`
```

## One issue, from its label to the base branch

A repo holding one small Go package was bound to the team; its gate formats, vets and tests. One issue was opened with the label `flow:fix`: a named form the package was to read, with what each call should give written out. Nobody touched it again. One fleet instance on one laptop worked it, `concurrency: 3`:

```text
stage         role             harness      model                 worked    cost
workup        fellow           claude-code  fable                 1m 44s   $1.39
plan-review   attending        pi           openai-codex/gpt-5.5     51s   $0.41
treatment     fellow           claude-code  opus                  1m 06s   $0.45
code-review   attending        claude-code  opus                  1m 02s   $0.47
discharge     discharge-nurse  claude-code  sonnet                   28s   $0.14
the landing   discharge-nurse  claude-code  its default              31s   $0.19
```

From opened to merged on the base branch: 9 minutes 29 seconds and $3.05, with no rework and no human. The repo's two patrols, `triage` and `rounds`, ran three times beside it, for $0.23 more.

`worked` is a worker's session, from its first word to its last. The rest of the nine minutes is the fleet's: one tick reads a verdict and starts the next stage's worker, and a worker's `wake` ends the sleep between two. `cost` is what each harness reckoned for its session at its provider's listed prices: under a subscription login nothing is billed by the call.

Every stage left its record on the issue, a comment that names the harness it ran on beside the commits of the role and of the team it ran under:

```text
<!--convoy:stage stage=plan-review verdict=pass … harness=pi-->
```

## What held the pi worker

The issue asked the plan's reviewer to try one commit, so that the refusal could be seen. pi made the call, it was refused, and the worker quoted the refusal in the text of its verdict:

```text
afkconvoy guard: the stage `plan-review` is marked `writes: false`: `git commit`
is refused. A stage that writes nothing leaves no commit and pushes nothing; say
what you found in the text of your verdict
```

That is the fleet's guard, which a pi worker asks through the extension the fleet adds to it (`afkconvoy run --help`). It answered before the role's own limits were reached, so `limits.ts` refused nothing in this run: it is what refuses the same commit in a stage a workflow left unmarked. Its other limit was met and let the worker through — the reviewer read the `SKILL.md` of both skills its skill names before it declared `pass`.

### `afkconvoy help cache`

The one directory of its own the fleet keeps on a host: where it is, what moves it, and what it holds. The helps that speak of a file under "the cache directory" mean this one.

## Where it is

- `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/afkconvoy`: where XDG_CACHE_HOME is set and not empty
- `$HOME/.cache/afkconvoy`: otherwise — on macOS too: never ~/Library/Caches

It is made when something is first kept in it. With neither variable set, a command that needs it fails and says so.

## What moves it

Setting XDG_CACHE_HOME, and nothing else: there is no flag and no config key for it. To keep everything under a directory of your choosing:

```sh
XDG_CACHE_HOME="$PWD/.cache" afkconvoy check
```

Each command reads the variable for itself, so two commands find the same copies and the same log only under the same value: a `doctor` run without the one a `run` was started with reads another directory, and finds no log there. The host runner keeps the directory of the `run` that started it, whatever its login shell sets, and so does every fleet instance it holds; a `run` under another value asks the host runner of that directory, and starts one there where none answers.

## What it holds

- `copies/`: the fleet's copy of a team's repo and of each role's, one per commit, read-only: copies/<owner>/<repo>/<commit>. A worker of a bound repo starts in one; an unbound repo has none.
- `harness/`: the user directory the fleet keeps for pi and for Codex, a worker's in place of yours: harness/pi, harness/codex.
- `runs/`: the tick log of each repo's fleet instance, one file per repo: what `doctor` reads. It keeps every line of the last 24 hours, and never fewer than 200 lines nor more than 5000, the oldest dropped first.
- `checkouts.json`: the checkout list, the checkouts the host runner works, each with the `--instance`, `--host` and `--worker-no-proxy` its `run` named, and beside them the host settings (`afkconvoy run --help`); `checkouts.lock`, held while it is changed.
- `host-runner.lock`: held by the host runner as long as it runs, so a host has one; it says its pid, its version and when it started.
- `host-runner.sock`: the host runner's socket, the one socket of the host: `run`, `stop`, `wake`, `panel --open` and `doctor` speak to the host runner there, each naming its checkout. No fleet instance and no repo has a socket of its own. One nobody listens on — a host runner killed with no goodbye left it — is removed by whoever finds it.
- `host-runner.log`: the host runner's log, moved aside to host-runner.log.1 once past a MiB: what it started, added, refused and stopped, each line stamped in UTC.
- `host-inspection/`: what the last inspection of the host was given (evidence.md) and what it found (last.json), whichever fleet of the host started it: what `doctor` and the panel show beside admission's reading.

None of it is fleet state: that is in GitHub and on the repo's remote.

## See also

- `afkconvoy check --help`: when a copy is cloned, and what is read from it
- `afkconvoy run --help`: the log, and what each harness's user directory holds
- `afkconvoy doctor --help`: what is read back from the log and the copies

### `afkconvoy help tick-log`

What every command that acts does as it ends, whoever runs it: the line it adds to the tick log, and the fleet instance it wakes. A command's own `--help` says, under "What it logs", that it is one.

## The line it logs

As it acts it appends one line to the tick log of this host for this repo — the command, what it acted on, who ran it (a worker or the operator) and how it came out, or that it failed — whether a `run` is there or not:

```
park #46 (operator): blocked by #99
verdict #121 (worker): FAILED: issue #121 is closed
```

## The fleet instance it wakes

Then it wakes this host's fleet instance of this repo, asking the host runner on its socket, naming its checkout: the fleet instance logs `woken by park #46` and starts its next tick, or follows the one in progress with it. It waits 3 seconds at most for the answer, which says whether it woke one, as "woke". With no host runner, or none holding a fleet instance of this repo, it does nothing more.

Both are soft: a command acts the same whether either can be done, and with no fleet instance to wake its line is in the log all the same.

### `afkconvoy help worker-proxy`

Which hosts a worker reaches past the proxy: a setting of one start on one host, said by `--worker-no-proxy`, which `run`, `tick`, `dispatch`, `restart` and `switch` take to start workers with, and `plan` and `doctor` to show what such a start would do. It is never a key of the repo's config: no proxy setting is read from the config or written to GitHub.

## The flag

`--worker-no-proxy [HARNESS=]HOSTS` says a comma-separated list of hosts workers reach directly. The bare form is for the default harness; repeat it for other harnesses, never twice for one.

```
--worker-no-proxy dsh=api.deepseek.com,internal.example
```

## What a worker is given

The worker's login shell extends its exported no_proxy and NO_PROXY with this list and exports the joined list under both names before it starts the worker. Every other proxy variable stays as it was. Without a list, both spellings stay untouched, except DSH's stock api.deepseek.com addition. Say `--worker-no-proxy dsh=` to turn that stock addition off. These settings apply to every worker, including patrols, consults and the train worker.

## What `plan` and `doctor` show

Each answers `worker_no_proxy` — `doctor` under `host` — listing every harness: {harness, addition, no_proxy, NO_PROXY}. `addition` is the host list added, null when none is: a null addition leaves both inherited values alone. The other fields show the login shell's resulting comma-separated values. They describe a start now, with the flags given to that command and the host user's login shell exports.

### `afkconvoy help humans`

Every way the fleet stops for a human, and the command that answers each.

## Where to look

`afkconvoy doctor` lists every open issue that waits for a human under `waiting_on_human`, with why, since when and `answer`: the line to run for that issue. `afkconvoy plan` gives the same list; the panel shows it as "With a human". Waiting more than an hour is a finding.

An escalated issue carries the escalate label (`ready-for-human` unless renamed) in place of its flow label. Its comment says why and ends with the line to answer. Run every command below in a checkout of the repo.

## An escalation

A stage failed or declared `escalate`. Its consult — the stock consult where none is named, and in an unbound repo — was asked first and let it through, unless the stage says `escalate: { to: human }` or the config `escalate_to: human`. The comment says what failed or gives the question that needs your answer.

For a failure, fix what failed first: `afkconvoy rule` starts the same stage anew, and what failed it once fails it again. In an unbound repo there is no stage to run again: fix what the comment names and put the ready label back, with the line the comment ends with. A PR the escalation kept is not started anew: the next worker takes it up — it reads the issue's comments, merges the base branch, gates and joins the landing train — so say on the issue what is to be done on it.

## Answering an escalation

Every command a human runs to answer one, `<n>` the issue's number. A consult may run each, and any read-only command, the gate too; never commit, push or change the host.

- `afkconvoy rule --issue <n> --text-file <file>`: The stage runs again under your ruling; both rework counts start over (a consult's starts none over). `afkconvoy rule --help`.
- `afkconvoy send --issue <n> --stage <stage> --text-file <file>`: Put it at another stage, when the approach or workflow changed, or bring it back from a park. `afkconvoy send --help`.
- `gh issue close <n> --comment <why>`: Nothing is left to do on it: the fleet leaves a closed issue alone.
- `gh issue create --title <title> --body-file <file> --label <ready label>`: Open what it found outside this issue — a broken base branch, a host problem, a defect of afkconvoy — for the fleet to work.
- `gh issue edit <n> --body-file <file>`: Keep its body's "## Blocked by" in step with an edge added or removed.
- `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/<n>/dependencies/blocked_by -F issue_id=<id>`: Record it as blocked by the issue whose database id is `<id>`.
- `gh api -X DELETE repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/<n>/dependencies/blocked_by/<id>`: Remove that edge: one whose waiting would never end, say.

## Parked for evidence

A consult's close or park carries a reason and adds no rework. `plan` and `doctor` list parks under `waiting_on_human`. To bring one back in a bound repo, explicitly send it with new evidence or your reason (a plain comment does not bring it back):

```sh
afkconvoy send --issue <n> --stage <stage> --text-file <evidence-file>
```

In an unbound repo, comment with the evidence, then restore its ready label:

```sh
gh issue edit <n> --add-label <ready label> --remove-label convoy:parked
```

## A tripped breaker

Rework went past what the workflow allows — in total, or as rejections in a row by one stage — and the issue went to the consult in place of that rework, and to a human where the stage says `to: human` or it trips again after the consult ruled. The comment names the breaker and lists every rework with its stage and why. Answer as an escalation: `afkconvoy rule` with what settles it, or `afkconvoy send`. `afkconvoy doctor` says beforehand when an issue is one rework from a breaker.

## A stage `by: human`

A workflow may give a stage to a human. An issue at one waits there, claimed by nobody, under its flow label and with no escalate label: only the lists above show it.

- `afkconvoy verdict pass --issue <n> --stage <stage> --text-file <file>`: Declare the stage's verdict: `pass`, or `reject` where the stage has that edge. The issue goes where the workflow leads from it. `afkconvoy verdict --help`.

## A patrol's failed run

A run of a patrol that failed opens an issue of its own, under the escalate label, which says what failed. The patrol is not run again while that issue is open.

- `gh issue close <n>`: Once you have looked: the patrol runs again when it is next due. `afkconvoy plan` gives each patrol's standing.

## A fleet lock

An open issue under the lock label is a fleet lock: the fleet works lock issues only, and hands no other issue to a human, until the last one closes. A worker raises one when the fault is one every issue shares; a human may too:

```sh
afkconvoy lock --issue <n>
```

Closing a lock's issue ends it. A lock needs you when nothing can work its issue: it has no flow label or an open blocker. `afkconvoy doctor` gives a critical finding with a `fix` to run. Close a lock raised by mistake. `afkconvoy lock --help`.

## A precedent to accept

Where the team names who proposes precedents, each ruling a human gives with `afkconvoy rule` is followed by a proposal: a PR on the team's repo that appends one entry to its precedents — the ruling in a sentence, when it applies, and a link to the ruling. Nothing waits on it: the stage that asked has already run again.

- `gh pr merge <pr> --repo <the team's repo>`: Merging accepts the precedent: every later stage reads it, and follows it in place of declaring `escalate` on the same question.
- `gh pr close <pr> --repo <the team's repo>`: The ruling was about that one issue, and no stage should follow it unasked.

The fleet never merges on the team's repo. `afkconvoy plan` lists the proposals under way and open under `proposals`.

## An issue past the end of its workflow

A workflow that ended without a landing leaves its issue open: `gh issue close <n>`.

## What not to do

Do not move the labels by hand: an issue's stage records say where it is, so one handed back with no ruling on record is escalated again. Rule on it, or send it.

### `afkconvoy help troubleshooting`

Start with `afkconvoy doctor`, in the checkout the fleet runs in: it reads everything and changes nothing. Each finding has a `fix` — a line to run, or a file and key to edit — and `evidence`. Below, a row for each: the words its `what` holds, why, and what to do. Then what a start refuses with, and what neither says.

## What `doctor` finds — critical: the fleet does not work until it is fixed

- `is not installed`: A command the fleet needs is not on this host. Run `fix`: the line that installs it.
- `is not logged in`: `gh` or `claude` is logged out, as a login shell sees it. Run `fix`. Of `codex`: it has no login in ~/.codex/auth.json, the file a worker is given. One Codex keeps in a keyring is in no file: have Codex keep it in one, and run `fix`.
- `holds credentials for no provider`: A stage or a patrol runs on pi, logged in nowhere. Start `pi` and type `/login`.
- `is not running`: orca is not running, and every worker is started through it. Run `fix`.
- `cannot be asked about this checkout`: orca runs but did not say which repos it knows; `evidence` says why. Run `fix`.
- `does not know this checkout`: orca was never given the checkout worktrees are cut from. Run `fix`, once.
- `cannot start a worker`: The first word of a worker launch command resolves to nothing in a login shell, as an alias of your own shell's may. Name one that does: `afkconvoy run --help`.
- `cannot start a worker in its role`: In a bound repo the worker launch command must end in its harness, taking flags: the fleet adds what puts the worker in its role. `afkconvoy run --help`.
- ``no `afkconvoy run` is alive``: The `run` of this host died holding claims. Start it here: it takes them back.
- `is broken`: This checkout's fleet instance panicked, its loop ended in an error, or its startup probe no longer passes; every other goes on, and the host runner starts it again after a backoff, when `evidence` says. Put right what `what` says, then run `fix`: a `run` starts it at once.
- `failed in each of the last`: One step fails tick after tick; `evidence` is its error, naming what refused. `fix`.
- `the team this repo names cannot be read`: The team's repo, or a role's, could not be read. `afkconvoy check` says which.
- `has a fault at its head`: A team's or a role's file is wrong on its default branch. `fix` is the file and key; `afkconvoy check` gives every fault. Push the edit: no stage starts until then.
- `stands and cannot be worked`: A fleet lock is on an issue no worker can be started on, so the fleet works nothing. `fix` gives the issue what it lacks; [`afkconvoy help humans`](help:humans).
- `the fleet's state cannot be read`: GitHub, the remote or the config failed to answer; `evidence` says which.
- `harness is down`: Identical refusals hold claims and pause it; a prompt probes every 5m. Run `fix`.

## What `doctor` finds — warning: one issue or one patrol is held up

A warning may be the fleet mid-step: run `doctor` again after a tick before you act on one.

- `has no worker`: A claim's worker is gone; a tick starts one. `fix` is for a claim it leaves so.
- `has been stopped for`: A worker stopped half an hour ago and declared nothing: read its terminal; `fix`.
- `the last tick started no worker`: Slots are free, the frontier is not empty, and nothing was dispatched: `evidence` is the tick's line, and `fix` the step that failed or the dispatch by hand.
- `follows no workflow of the team`: An issue's flow label names no workflow, or it has two. `afkconvoy flows` lists all.
- `longer than any stage before it took`: Nothing is wrong yet: an issue has been at one stage for long. `fix` shows it.
- `is one rework from a breaker`: The next `reject` escalates the issue. Nothing to do yet: [`afkconvoy help humans`](help:humans).
- `is paused on this host`: It refused every prompt: no worker starts on it till an hourly probe answers.
- `names no model the host kit holds`: A team's roster names a model by a name that matches no model the host kit holds for its harness, by its id or any other name; `evidence` gives the nearest names. The fleet never changes a roster: a tick opens one issue for it in the team's repo, which the team's own fleet works. `fix` is the file and key to correct.
- `has no harness on this host it holds limits for`: A role holds limits for no harness the host kit holds, so no worker of it starts and its stages wait; the rest go on. They go on by themselves once the host kit holds one: `afkconvoy kit`, or write the role's limits for one it holds.
- `matches nothing in the host kit`: A role's roster entry names only harnesses or models this host lacks, so the role runs the host kit whole, less what it holds no limits for. Add one with `afkconvoy kit`, or change the roster.
- `does not run: its last run failed`: The issue that reports a patrol's failed run is open. Look, then close it: `fix`.
- `` have reached its `max_open` ``: A patrol is not run while that many of its issues are open. Close some, or raise it.
- `has waited for a human for`: Nothing in the fleet moves that issue. `fix` answers it: [`afkconvoy help humans`](help:humans).
- `is held off by a PR not the fleet's`: No worker starts: it would open a second PR. `fix` closes it, or merge it yourself.
- `is claimed but GitHub has it no more`: Deleted or transferred: its fleet's next tick releases it. `fix` is for one stopped.
- `the gate is slow`: On one host, the last 5 landings with a recorded gate run all took more than 80% of the gate limit. A tick opens one issue for the fleet to make the gate faster: `fix` shows it. Raising `gate_seconds` is no fix, nor is deleting or skipping tests.

## What `doctor` finds — info: nothing is held up

- `moved since the stage`: A role or the team was pushed after a stage started: that worker goes by the older one, the next stage by the head. `afkconvoy doctor --help` says what moved is.
- `declares no gate limit`: The config sets no `gate_seconds`: the gate may run 3600 seconds before anything ends it. Set it to the most the gate should take: `fix` names the file and key.
- `is kept with no claim`: A worktree holds what the remote lacks, or an earlier release kept it. `fix` removes it, pushing first what only it holds: read `what` before you run it.

## What a start refuses with — `plan`, `tick` and `run` check first, and start nothing

- `this host cannot work a fleet yet`: What `doctor` finds on a host, said at once: run each line after a colon.
- `cannot read the config file`: The repo has no config on the branch checked out. `afkconvoy config --help`.
- `the remote has no branch`: The config's `base_branch` is not on the remote. Push it: the fleet creates none.
- `that push would be refused`: The base branch's protection requires a PR, checks or a named pusher, and the landing train lands by pushing. Lift the rule, or pick another base branch.
- `the remote rejects the fleet's refs under both`: The remote takes neither hidden refs nor `convoy-*` branches, so no claim can be kept. A push rule of the remote's is what refuses: lift it for one of the two.
- `the host kit has no worker launch command`: Run `afkconvoy kit` on this host: it holds every harness found and answering there. One it leaves out is in its `left_out`, with why.
- `cannot read the host kit`: Run `afkconvoy kit` on this host, or `run`, which writes it where there is none.
- `--worker-command is gone`: Run `afkconvoy kit` to edit this host's worker launch commands.
- `is no harness`: Use claude-code, pi, codex or dsh.

## What neither says

- **An issue is not worked**: `afkconvoy plan` has it under `excluded`, with why. Remove what the reason names.
- **A changed role or team did not reach a worker**: It is not pushed to its default branch, or the stage had already started.
- **The labels were moved back, and the issue escalated again**: A label is not where an issue is: [`afkconvoy help humans`](help:humans).
- **A stage's verdict counted for nothing**: Its record names another stage than its claim was for. `afkconvoy show --issue <n>` says how each record was read; `afkconvoy send` puts the issue where it belongs.
- **Another host's fleet died**: Its claims go stale by themselves and are taken. Or: `afkconvoy takeover --help`.
- **Everything must stop now**: SIGTERM the host runner (`host_runner.pid` in any `run`'s answer), then close the workers' terminals in orca. Every issue keeps its labels and stage records: a later `run` goes on from where each one was.

### `afkconvoy help glossary`

# afkconvoy

A command-line tool that works a repo's ready GitHub-issue backlog unattended: it dispatches one worktree-isolated coding agent per issue and lands their finished PRs on the base branch behind a local gate. It is a trimmed Rust port of the `afk-fleet` skill (`docs/adr/0001`).

## Language

### The fleet

**Fleet instance**:
One repo's fleet in its host's host runner, and everything it owns: the workers it started and the claims it holds, under an id minted when it starts. One host runs at most one per repo.
_Avoid_: launcher, coordinator, node, process (the host runner is the process)

**Host runner**:
A host's one long-running process of the fleet, holding a fleet instance for each checkout on its host's checkout list. `run` starts it in the background where none runs, and adds its checkout to it either way. `stop` takes one checkout off its list, and `stop --all`, or SIGTERM, stops it and keeps the list.
_Avoid_: daemon (a process outside the fleet), server (an MCP server, a model provider's), supervisor

**Checkout list**:
The checkouts a host's runner works, kept on that host and never pushed. The host runner converges on it: a checkout added is started, and a host runner started again starts every checkout on it.
_Avoid_: registry, workspace list, projects (Codex's config key)

**Broken**:
A fleet instance whose loop panicked or ended in an error, or that the host runner started again, with nobody asking, and that ended before its first tick — its startup probe no longer passing, say. It harms no other and stays on the checkout list: the host runner starts it again after a backoff — a minute, twice as long at each break in a row, half an hour at the most — or at once when a `run` of its checkout asks. It is **back** once such a start ended its first tick. A tick that fails is no break: the loop goes on.
_Avoid_: crashed, dead (a heartbeat past the lease), down (a harness that refuses every prompt)

**Host settings**:
What a host says for every fleet instance on it — whether it may be put to sleep and its sleep hours, the limits past which a worker is hot, the shares admission holds back at, the panel's port — kept beside the checkout list and changed by any `run` that names one, for every fleet instance on the host at once.
_Avoid_: global config, runner flags

**Tick**:
One reconciliation pass: rebuild the working set from fleet state, then perform every transition it calls for, without waiting for the workers it started.
_Avoid_: cycle, poll, batch

**Plan**:
A tick stopped after its rebuild, which reports what an acting tick would do and leaves nothing written: its startup probe, when it makes one, is the only thing it pushes, and it deletes that.
_Avoid_: dry run, preview

**Startup probe**:
What `run`, `tick` and `plan` ask of a host and a repo before anything else: that every command the fleet needs is installed and logged in, that orca is running and knows the checkout, that the base branch exists and no rule of its protection refuses a push, where the remote takes the fleet's refs, and whether it takes recorded gate runs. A host or a repo the fleet cannot work is refused here, not at its first tick or landing. `run` makes one at every start; one that passed stands for an hour on the host that made it, and `tick` and `plan` make none while it does.
_Avoid_: bootstrap, preflight, health check

**Ref layout**:
One of the two ways every ref the fleet writes is named: hidden refs (`refs/convoy/*`), or — only where the remote rejects those — ordinary branches (`convoy-*`), on which push-triggered CI fires.
_Avoid_: namespace, fallback mode

**Fleet state**:
The authoritative record of what is claimed, in flight, landed, parked and escalated. It lives entirely in GitHub; no process holds it.
_Avoid_: run state, memory (what a host holds resident, as under Hot worker)

**Working set**:
A tick's view of the fleet at one moment, derived from fleet state and dropped when the tick ends.
_Avoid_: session state

**Rebuild**:
The read-only pass at the top of every tick that derives the working set. Any fleet instance rebuilds the same working set from the same GitHub. It lists the remote once and asks GitHub a fixed number of times, however many issues are open.
_Avoid_: refresh (a heartbeat is refreshed), resync

**Frontier**:
The issues a worker can be started on now: open, carrying a flow label, not an epic, unclaimed, with no open blocker, and at a stage a role performs or whose `escalate` a consult is to rule on — or landing, with an open PR to join. In an unbound repo: carrying the ready label, with no open linked PR but one of the fleet's own that a released claim kept, off the landing train — which its worker takes up. While a fleet lock stands: of these, the lock issues only.
_Avoid_: queue (the exclusive queue of a host's heavy commands), backlog (all the issues a repo has open)

**Idle**:
A fleet instance with nothing to do now: it holds no claim — on an issue, a patrol's run or the proposal of a precedent — nothing is on its landing train, and its frontier is empty. An escalated issue waiting for a human leaves it idle, and so does a patrol not yet due.
_Avoid_: drained, done (what a step or a command did), finished (a PR its worker is through with)

**Host sleep**:
A fleet instance putting its host to sleep: the host's local time is within its sleep hours, every fleet instance on the host has been idle for ten minutes, each has ticked once more and found nothing, no one has used the host's keyboard or mouse for ten minutes, the one that puts it to sleep has worked since the host last woke, and the host settings do not keep it awake. A host woken stays awake until some instance on it has worked again. The fleet never wakes a host: one put to sleep within its sleep hours sleeps on past their end.
_Avoid_: sleep (the wait between ticks), hibernate, suspend, shutdown

**Sleep hours**:
The hours of a host's local time its fleets may put it to sleep in: from 00:00 to 06:00 unless its host settings say others (`--host-sleep-hours 22:00-06:00`), the start included and the end not, past midnight where the end comes first, and any hour with `00:00-24:00`. A check for host sleep outside them keeps the host awake, says so, and is followed by the next as they start.
_Avoid_: quiet hours, night mode

**Base branch**:
The one branch a repo's fleet work is cut from and lands on.
_Avoid_: trunk, main, default branch (a team's or a role's repo is read at its own)

### Teams and roles

**Role**:
A directory that defines one kind of worker: the rules it always works under, the limits it cannot cross, and the skills it can be asked to perform. It is a whole repo or a subdirectory of one. A worker starts in it, and is given nothing else of its repo.
_Avoid_: agent (as under Worker), persona, profile (as under DSH profile)

**Team**:
A directory that names a set of roles and holds the workflows, patrols and precedents they work by. It is a whole repo or a subdirectory of one, and its roles may be directories of the same repo.
_Avoid_: org, crew, squad

**Team rules**:
The rules every role of a team works under, whatever its own rules add. They say how the team works, and hold in any repo bound to it; what one codebase asks is that repo's to say, and what one kind of worker does is its role's.
_Avoid_: global rules, shared rules

**Admission**:
Whether a tick starts new workers on its host: not while the host is past a share of its load, under memory pressure, or low on free disk under the checkout. What it holds back stays on the frontier for the next tick; workers already running, the landing train and the worker a declared verdict starts are never held back. The shares have defaults taken from the host's cores, memory and disk, and the host can say its own in its host settings. Holding back for one reason — the load, memory or disk — at every tick past a span (ten minutes, or the host's own) starts an inspection of the host, once an **episode**: the episode ends once admission has admitted for five minutes. Holding back for reasons that change starts none.
_Avoid_: throttling, backpressure

**Host user's skills and rules**:
The skills and the rules the host's own user has for a harness, which a session they start by hand loads: a worker of a bound repo is given them beside its role's, unless its team file says `host_user: false`. A role may say it for itself, whatever the team says: `reviewer: { dir: ./roles/reviewer, host_user: false }` in `roles`; a role named by its directory alone takes the team's. Its role's skills win over them, and the brief, its role's rules, the team rules and the repo's own rules win over theirs. DSH alone may load those too when its role chooses the host user's DSH profile.
_Avoid_: global rules, user config, personal skills

**DSH profile**:
What a DSH worker loads of bundles, plugins, MCP servers, patches, themes and settings: the fleet's own (`dsh_profile: fleet`, the default), or the host user's `dsh-tui` profile (`dsh_profile: host-user`). The team chooses for every role; a role may choose its own, independently of `host_user`, and both keep the guard and the role's limits.
_Avoid_: provider profile, persona

**Bound repo**:
A repo whose config names a team. An unbound repo has no roles and one fixed path for every issue: one worker, then the landing train.
_Avoid_: team mode, managed repo

**Guard**:
The check made before each thing a worker does, refusing what its role or its stage may not do. It stops a worker that errs, not one that means to get past it.
_Avoid_: permission (what a harness's own settings deny), sandbox (what a harness may shut a worker's commands in)

### Workflows

**Workflow**:
The stages one issue passes through and where each verdict leads, ending in the landing train or in nothing more to do.
_Avoid_: pipeline, process (a program that is running)

**Flow label**:
The label that names the workflow an issue follows: `flow:<name>`, unless the workflow's file names another with `label` — the ready label, say, so that an issue opened the usual way is worked. A bound repo's issue is the fleet's to work only while it carries one; there the ready label is one only where a workflow names it.
_Avoid_: type label

**Intake**:
Putting a flow label on an issue. A human does it on GitHub; a worker does it through the fleet, which records who did and holds the number of such issues still open under a limit.
_Avoid_: enroll, admit (a tick starting new workers on a host not busy: admission), triage

**Stage**:
One step of a workflow: one skill of one role, performed by one new worker — or a decision waited for from a human.
_Avoid_: step (one thing a tick does), phase, state (fleet state and worker state are terms)

**Stage record**:
The comment a stage leaves on its issue: what it produced, its verdict, the versions of the role and team it ran under, and the harness its worker ran on, with the model where it was started on one. A human who declares for a stage, rules on it or sends the issue to it leaves one too, which says a human did; so does the fleet, for a stage that runs again because a fleet lock closed. The stage an issue is at is derived from these and stored nowhere.
_Avoid_: handoff note, log (the tick log; what a gate prints), stage label

**Position**:
Where an issue is in its workflow: at a stage a worker is to perform, waiting on a human, with a consult, parked, landing, ended, or escalating. It is derived from the stage records each tick and stored nowhere.
_Avoid_: state (as under Stage), status (the status board; a key of what a command answers), current stage

**Rework**:
A stage running again because a later stage rejected its work or a consult ruled on it. It is counted per issue from the stage records, from where a human last ruled on the issue or sent it to a stage.
_Avoid_: retry, round, attempt (what an issue was worked into before a fresh start)

**Breaker**:
A limit on rework — in total for an issue, or as rejections in a row by one stage — past which the issue escalates.
_Avoid_: retry limit, circuit

**Consult**:
A worker in a more senior role, asked before a human is whenever its stage would hand the issue to a human — an `escalate` verdict, a failure, a tripped breaker, a workflow changed under the issue. It stands where that human stands: told what the human would be, and free to run what a human answering runs. It rules, sends the issue to a stage, closes it, or lets it through; it commits, pushes and changes the host never. The same hand-off again, and its own failure, go to a human. Where a stage names none, and in an unbound repo, the **stock consult** stands in: afkconvoy's own, in no role of a team, whose one instruction is to decide as the human would. A stage that says `escalate: { to: human }`, or an unbound repo whose config says `escalate_to: human`, has no consult.
_Avoid_: review (a stage may be named it), second opinion, handoff, default consult

**Ruling**:
What a consult or a human decides on an issue handed on. The stage runs again under it; a human's also hands the issue back to the fleet and starts the rework counts over, a consult's starts none over.
_Avoid_: answer (what a command prints), decision (what a `by: human` stage waits for), override

**Precedent**:
A ruling kept so that later stages follow it instead of escalating. A worker proposes it; a human accepts it.
_Avoid_: rule (a role's rules and the team rules; the command `rule`), policy, guideline

**Proposal**:
One human's ruling put forward as a precedent: a PR on the team's repo that appends one entry to its precedents file. A ruling gets one; a human merging it is what accepts the precedent.
_Avoid_: suggestion, draft (a roster `afkconvoy draft` writes), candidate (a key of what `recovery` answers)

**Split**:
Parking an issue on issues its own stage opened. When they have all closed, that stage runs again and judges the whole.
_Avoid_: decompose, epic (an issue under an epic label), fan out

**Patrol**:
A role run on a schedule rather than for an issue. It opens issues and takes them in; it writes no code. It is due once its interval has passed since its last run, and — where its file says `max_runs_a_day` — while fewer than that many of its runs started in the last 24 hours, rolling. Where it says `max_landed_a_day`, it is also held while that many issues it opened were closed as completed in the last rolling 24 hours, until enough completions are 24 hours old to fall below the bound. Its run takes one slot until its worker declares it over, which the next tick acts on; a worker that never does is ended once it is gone or has stopped for a grace period. Each run has a checkout of its own, removed as the run ends unless it failed.
_Avoid_: cron, job, scheduled worker

**Fleet lock**:
An open issue carrying the lock label, in a bound repo or an unbound one. While one stands the fleet works lock issues only — nothing else is dispatched, no PR of another issue joins the landing train, and workers already running are left alone, what they declare being acted on afterwards — and closing the last one ends it. A stage's `escalate` or failure the lock explains — declared before it closed, and not acted on since — is then not carried out: the stage runs again, which is no rework.
_Avoid_: freeze, pause (a harness paused on a host, as under Host kit), kill switch

### Workers

**Harness**:
The program a worker is a session of: it runs a model, with tools, on the work it is handed. Claude Code is one, pi another, Codex the third, and DeepSeek Harness (DSH) the fourth. An issue's casting names the one its workers run, within their role's range; the host kit names the stock consult's. A host where a switch chose one starts every worker of the repo on that one.
_Avoid_: agent (as under Worker), coding agent (as under Worker), CLI, provider (whose models a harness runs)

**Roster**:
A team's list, for each of its roles, of the harnesses and models that role's workers may run, in order of preference, with what each model is good at and how an issue is to be cast among them. It is committed with the team, written under the team file's `roster`: for each role it names, a `run` listing `{ harness, model, good_at }` in that order of preference — a harness named with no model allows any model the host kit holds for it — and a `cast` saying how to cast among them. A role's **range** on a host is its entry cut to the host kit, in the roster's order, less each harness the role holds no limits for while it holds limits for another; a role it names no entry for ranges over the host kit, less the same — and so does one whose entry matches nothing in the host kit, which `check`, `plan` and `doctor` name — and an unbound repo, having no team, over the host kit whole. A role whose range is empty, holding limits for no harness the host kit holds, refuses no start: no worker of it is started, its stages wait while it lasts, and every other stage goes on. A stage, a patrol and a config name no harness and no model: what a worker runs is its role's range's to say. A roster is drafted by `afkconvoy draft` from a host kit into the team's working tree — every role, every harness and model in the host kit's order, what the host kit's first model says each is good at and how to cast — and committed by a human; the fleet never changes it. An entry that names a model the host kit holds by no name is named with the nearest names and given one issue in the team’s repo for its own fleet to correct.
_Avoid_: harness config, model table, routing rules

**Host kit**:
The harnesses and models one host can start now — each harness's worker launch command, each model it was seen to answer with, in order of preference, and the harness and model of its stock consult. A model is held once per harness, by its **id** — the model its probe answered as, which a worker is started on — with its other **names**: each name its harness lists that answered as it, and the name its harness shows it by. Claude Code's `opus`, `default` and `Opus 5.5` are `claude-opus-5-5`; pi's `openai-codex/gpt-6-sol` and Codex's `gpt-6-sol` are one model on two harnesses, with one `good_at`, its dated source URLs in **sources** and the time it was researched in **researched_at**. After probing, a headless research session on the host kit's first searches primary and high-trust sources for new answered identities alone, and its checked answer gives their strengths and weaknesses and preference order. Missing or unsourced findings are `not researched` and stay in their fixed place; an invalid answer or fifteen-minute timeout keeps the fixed order and held research. A held identity keeps its research indefinitely, and with no new identity no session starts. A model named anywhere — a roster entry, a `model:` label, the stock consult — matches the model of its harness whose id or name it is, whatever the case, or with the provider prefix left off where that leaves one match; a name with two matches matches neither. The fleet writes ids. `afkconvoy kit` — or `run`, on a host with none — writes it with no human: it finds each harness installed in the shell a worker gets, asks it for its models, sends each a one-line prompt, and keeps those that answered, with how long they took and when; the harnesses it held keep their order, new ones follow in a fixed order of harnesses, and each one's models are in the order it lists them. Its **first** is its first harness on that harness's first model, which the stock consult runs where the host kit names none for it. It stays current with no human: once a day a tick of one fleet of the host writes it again, adding a model a harness now lists once it answers its probe and dropping one it no longer lists, and the others read what it wrote; a harness that stops answering is kept, and paused. Kept on that host and never pushed; a harness paused on the host is left out of it until it works again.
_Avoid_: roster (the team's), host config, inventory

**Casting**:
The harness and model an issue's workers run, named by the issue's `harness:` and `model:` labels — and the act of choosing them, by a human or by a caster. A stage whose range holds the casting runs it, one whose range does not runs its range's first, and one whose range holds one harness and one model runs that, whatever the casting; a name that matches nothing never stops work: a casting none of an issue's stages' ranges holds runs each stage's range's first, `unmatched`, and the issue is told once which label matched nothing, what ran instead and what the host kit holds; an issue none of whose stages has a choice to make is not cast. In an unbound repo the host kit is the range: its worker runs the casting where the host kit holds it, and the host kit's first where the issue has none or one it does not hold. A harness named with no model starts its command as written. A label a human put on is never recast or taken off: while it matches nothing it is not followed, and once the host kit holds it, it is again. A caster’s label whose model the host kit holds by no name is cast again.
_Avoid_: assignment (a GitHub assignee), routing, dispatch (starting a worker)

**Caster**:
A worker in no role that casts, in one session, every open issue of the repo's that carries a flow label, has a choice to make and no casting, by the roster and the host kit. A tick that finds such an issue on the frontier and no caster running starts one, which runs `afkconvoy cast` on the host kit's first; the tick holds those issues back while it runs, for ten minutes at most from its start, and dispatches what it did not cast uncast, on its range's first. A human runs the same casting with `afkconvoy cast`.
_Avoid_: assigner, router, dispatcher

**Worker**:
A session of one harness, started in one role to perform one stage of one issue — or, after its last stage, to join its PR to the landing train — in that issue's worktree, and to report through GitHub. In an unbound repo it has no role and owns its issue from start to landing. It is ended — its terminal closed — by the step that ends what it was started for: its stage, its claim, or its run.
_Avoid_: agent (whoever reads the help; and a worker, to whoever has not met the term), subagent, child (an issue a split opened)

**Switch**:
Moving running work onto another harness in one command: the host's choice of harness for a repo, kept on that host and never pushed — whoever else works the repo runs the harness they have — and each worker named ended and one of that harness started in its place, in the same worktree, on the same branch, at the same stage, briefed to continue what is there. Every worker the host starts for the repo afterwards is of the chosen harness, whatever an issue's casting names, until a switch chooses again or the choice is cleared — `switch --clear` forgets it — and the casting stands again: every worker started afterwards, and each the clear names, runs what its range and casting say. The claim, the branch and the PR are untouched, the switch is recorded on the PR, and it is no restart, rework or nudge.
_Avoid_: harness change (what a new casting makes)

**Worker launch command**:
The shell string every worker of one harness is started with, in a fleet instance: one for each harness its workers run. The host kit says it, per harness, kept on the host at `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/afkconvoy/kit.json` or `$HOME/.config/afkconvoy/kit.json` and written by `afkconvoy kit`; a harness absent from it is refused; a start checks that of every harness it could be asked for, and starts no worker when one cannot be started. In an unbound repo it is opaque: the fleet never parses it, appends to it nothing but its harness's model flag where the worker runs a model — its issue's casting, the host kit's first, or the stock consult's — and only starts it — as every worker — under `nice`, with a `TMPDIR` of its worktree's own. In a bound repo the fleet adds to it what puts the worker in its role.
_Avoid_: agent command, provider profile

**Worker state**:
Whether a worker is busy or has stopped, as its harness reports it to the worker backend — or, where the backend has no report of it, as its terminal's last output shows. Stopped never means finished.
_Avoid_: liveness, status (as under Position)

**Verdict**:
What ends a stage, declared on the issue by whoever performed it: `pass`, `reject`, `blocked`, `already-satisfied`, or `escalate`. Opening a PR declares nothing.
_Avoid_: outcome (what a worker leaves on GitHub: its PR on the landing train, or its verdict), result, needs-human

**Silent worker**:
A worker that stopped, declared nothing, and for the grace period showed no sign of life — its terminal's output, a commit, a file touched, being started or nudged — while waiting on no background work of its own: a shell or a monitor it started that its harness shows still running, or a command of its in the exclusive queue. One waiting on such work is not silent until that work ends and it stays still past its nudge, or until it has waited longer than the gate limit.
_Avoid_: hung, idle (a fleet instance with nothing to do)

**Hot worker**:
A worker whose processes — every one started with its `TMPDIR`, and every one under those — take more than their share of the host, or whose worktree has outgrown its build. Its processes: more than half the host's cores (one at the least) held for two minutes, more than a quarter of its memory resident, the most of any worker while the host is under memory pressure, or more written to disk in ten minutes than a tenth of the disk free (a GiB at the least). Its worktree: what git ignores there past `OUTGROWN_TIMES` its **fresh build** and past `OUTGROWN_FLOOR` — the train worktree's rule, judged once its first green `afkconvoy gate` has recorded that fresh build. The host can say other limits in its host settings (`--hot-cores`, `--hot-memory`, `--hot-written`). `run` samples each worker every ten seconds, with no root, and measures its worktree every minute; one that has stayed under every limit for five minutes — its worktree back under the rule among them — stops being hot, and that ends its **episode**: hot again later is a new one. The landing train's gate runs are the fleet's own and no worker's.
_Avoid_: hog

**Inspection**:
A worker in the role of the consult of a hot worker's stage — the stock consult where the stage names none, at no stage, and in an unbound repo — started in a checkout of its own once per episode, and given what was taken down as that worker turned hot (its process tree, a `sample` of its hottest process, its resident memory over the last minutes, what its processes wrote, the largest directories of its worktree), the issue, the worktree and the hot worker's terminal. It finds the work wrong, that heavy, or what takes so much not the worker's, and says so with `afkconvoy inspected`; the fleet types the first two at the hot worker and leaves what it found as a comment on the issue that is no stage record. One runs on a host at a time, across its fleets, takes no slot of the `concurrency`, and has 15 minutes. It is held as a consult and hands nothing on; nobody inspects where the stage or the repo says `human`, and a worker hot again after its inspection is never escalated for it. An inspection of the **host** is started by admission instead, on no worker: the stock consult, given what was taken down as it started — admission's reading and shares; for disk, each of the host's worktrees of every fleet with its issue, its stage, whether a worker holds it and what it holds, the landing train's, the fleet's caches and the largest directories of the whole volume under the home folder outside them, found within five minutes; for load or memory, the process trees of each worker and of the train and the hottest processes outside them. It finds what holds it `reclaimable` — something under the home folder can be rebuilt, which its `afkconvoy inspected` frees once it has checked each path: what git ignores in a git checkout no process uses and no worker holds, never a file git tracks or a change no commit holds, a closed issue's worktree holding no change, a tool's cache; what cannot be rebuilt or is expensive to fetch again — model weights, downloads, media, Docker's images, a user's files — it names, and nothing deletes — `fleet` — the fleet's own shape outgrows the host, for which the fleet opens one issue with the escalate label, and none other while it is open — or `not-its`; the log, the panel and `doctor` show it beside admission's reading. Of either kind, one runs on a host at a time, and none where another fleet of the host inspected it in the episode.
_Avoid_: investigation, diagnosis

**Exclusive queue**:
The queue of the commands run through `afkconvoy exclusive` on one host, shared by every fleet on it whatever its repo: one runs at a time, in the order they asked, and the rest wait. A command whose process dies leaves it. A worker with a command in it is busy, not silent, for no longer than the gate limit.
_Avoid_: mutex, semaphore, heavy lock (the fleet lock is another thing)

**Nudge**:
The one line the fleet types at a silent worker with no outcome, telling it to carry on. Sent once per worker.
_Avoid_: ping, reminder, retry

**Restart**:
Replacing a silent worker with a new one in the same worktree and the same role, with its PR, branch and worktree untouched. Made once, and only for a worker that is joining the landing train.
_Avoid_: retry, re-dispatch

**Continuation**:
Recovering a claim whose worker died from the progress that survived: its worktree if still on this host, else its pushed branch, else a fresh start from the base branch.
_Avoid_: resume, checkpoint restore

**Wake**:
A signal that ends the sleep between ticks of its host's fleet instance early: every command that changes fleet state sends one as it ends — a worker's last among them, once its outcome is on GitHub — naming itself and what it acted on, and carrying no state. The `run` that hears it answers at once, naming the tick it starts or the tick in progress it follows.
_Avoid_: notification, callback, done signal

### Claims

**Claim**:
The atomic lock marking one issue as owned by one fleet instance. Its creation succeeds for exactly one instance. It takes one slot of the `concurrency` while its worker is at work, and none once a verdict is declared under it: it is still held until that verdict is acted on, and a worker started under it again takes a slot as any start does.
_Avoid_: assignee, assignment, lock (the fleet lock)

**Heartbeat**:
The timestamp a fleet instance publishes for itself while it holds claims, stamped with its host. A claim is live while its owner's heartbeat is within the lease. A `run` told to stop while it holds no claim removes its own; a start removes the dead ones that hold nothing: those of the instances it took from, its own host's past the lease, and anyone's older than a day.
_Avoid_: ping, keepalive

**Orphaned claim**:
A claim of this fleet instance with no PR and no live worker. It is recovered by continuation, never released.
_Avoid_: stuck issue, zombie

**Stale claim**:
Another fleet instance's claim whose heartbeat is past the lease. It is the only claim a fleet takes from another host unattended.
_Avoid_: dead claim, abandoned claim

**Takeover**:
Taking another fleet instance's claims — on issues, on patrols' runs, on proposals — without waiting for the lease. It happens unconditionally at start for claims stamped with this host, and by explicit command for another host's. A claim taken — by a takeover, or as a stale claim — is still the claim it was created as: what was declared under it stands.
_Avoid_: failover, stale reclaim

### Outcomes

**Park**:
Recording a dependency a worker discovered as a blocker on its issue and releasing the claim, so the frontier holds the issue back until the blocker closes.
_Avoid_: defer, snooze, hold (a fleet instance holds its claims)

**Escalate**:
Handing an issue to a human: the reason is commented, with the line that answers it, the flow label is swapped for the escalate label, and the claim is released. Every hand-off — a failure, a tripped breaker, an `escalate` verdict, a changed workflow — goes first to the consult where the stage names one, and escalates when the consult lets it through or where none is named; nothing is retried. The issue then waits for a human, with every other open issue only one can move: `plan`, `doctor` and the panel list them, each with its line.
_Avoid_: fail (what a command, a gate or one thing a tick does may), retry, give up (a landing train is given up: Abandon)

**Status board**:
The single comment on a claimed issue that shows a human how far along it is, and what the afkconvoy that works it was built from. It is rendered from fleet state and never read back.
_Avoid_: progress log, worklog

**Panel**:
The one web page that shows a human where every fleet of a host stands: the host itself, what waits for a human across its repos, and for each repo its workflows as the lines of their stages, the issues at work, queued and held back at each, and the landing train. The host runner serves it, made anew from what each tick read; it is never read back.
_Avoid_: dashboard, status page, status board (the comment on one issue), UI

**Tick log**:
The file a fleet instance keeps on its own host: one line as it starts, a line as each tick starts — with why: its timer, a wake and the command that sent it, the fleet instance's start, or a follow-up — and one as it ends — what it did, and what changed on GitHub or by another host since the tick before where it acted on that — plus the lines of the events that reached the fleet instance: a wake heard during a tick, a check for host sleep, the host waking, being told to stop. Every command that changes fleet state, whoever runs it, appends a line of its own to the file of its host and repo as it acts — the command, the issue, who ran it, and how it came out or that it failed — whether a fleet instance is there or not. Each line is appended whole, and only the fleet instance cuts the file back: it keeps every line of the last day, and never fewer than 200 lines nor more than 5000. It is a log and not fleet state: nothing reads it to decide what the fleet does.
_Avoid_: state file, journal, history

**Finding**:
One thing `doctor` says is wrong with the fleet on this host, with how bad it is, what shows it, its fix — a line to run, or a file and the key in it to edit — and the help topic that explains it. `doctor` fixes none itself.
_Avoid_: diagnosis, alert, warning (one of its severities), error (what a command that failed answers with)

### Landing

**Gate**:
The repo's build-and-test command. It is the only machine verification a change must pass before it lands.
_Avoid_: CI (what a push to an ordinary branch starts), checks (what `check` and the startup probe make), local CI

**Recorded gate run**:
The evidence that the gate passed on one committed tree, with how long the run took and on which host, made by the tool that saw the exit code and kept where every host can read it.
_Avoid_: gate cache, CI status

**Sync**:
Bringing a branch up to date by merging into it. Nothing is ever rebased.
_Avoid_: rebase, update branch

**Landing train**:
The one append-only line of merge commits ahead of the base branch that finished PRs join, one merge commit per PR.
_Avoid_: merge queue, merge batch, landing turn

**Join**:
Putting a finished PR on the landing train. In an unbound repo the worker that wrote it does; in a bound repo a new worker does, in the landing role its workflow names, after the last stage passed.
_Avoid_: merge (what git does to two branches, and a human to a proposal's PR), enqueue

**Train worker**:
The one worker per repo that gates the landing train's tip and pushes it to the base branch as a fast-forward. It holds no claim and wrote none of the PRs it lands.
_Avoid_: merger, integrator, batch worker

**Abandon**:
Giving up a landing train whose worker stayed silent, with nothing landed; its PRs join the next train.
_Avoid_: fail (as under Escalate), bisect
